reviewer: Simulated category judge (Claude), round three final verification, 11 October 2026. Not an official judge.

reasons: A1 1: No quality measurement or matched comparison exists. The paper says so honestly. A09 is adverse: 73 of 186 evaluation inputs overlap training, so no uplift can be claimed.

A2 2: The fine-tuning design, fixed-code rescoring and separation of deterministic and AI steps are credible originality. They are documented designs only. The fine-tuned model was not listed at inspection, and A01-A07 are local illustrations.

A3 2: Reusable prompts, training and A08 (59/59 utility tests, synthetic fixtures, no inference) show governance intent. There is no record of use over time, maintenance or adaptation after model or prompt changes.

A4 2: The 257 person-days and the 8-to-4-hour task are team-reported, attributed and correctly nested. There is no task ledger, approval record or retained-quality evidence, so 'quality maintained' is unsubstantiated.
A5 1: Assurance-team use is reported only. There is no stakeholder measure, satisfaction data or service-user outcome. The paper now correctly says purposes are not outcomes.
editorial_fixes: Section 1 grammar: 'The account narrative describes training associates then working on the account and established reusable prompts.' Replace with: 'The account narrative describes training for associates then working on the account and the establishment of reusable prompts.'
Section 2: 'Exhibits A05 to A07 show this local capability.' Replace with: 'Exhibits A05 to A07 show local interfaces in a fresh demonstration workspace; they do not show client runs.'

Section 2: 'assemble analysis and reporting across a Sonar estate containing more than 1,200 projects' overstates scope. Replace with: 'assemble analysis and reporting for a Sonar estate of more than 1,200 projects; the number of projects evaluated is not stated in the source.'
Section 3 is now thin against A3. Do not pad it with new claims. Shortening the heading to match the content is preferable to adding assertions.

Remove the internal portal and approval-function names from Section 4 if organiser confidentiality rules treat them as programme identifiers. Use 'internal benefits recording and delivery-leadership review' instead.
missing_evidence: Underlying task ledger for 125 + 132 person-days, with review deductions and approval provenance
Matched quality comparison (defect leakage, review rework or test-case adequacy) before and after AI assistance
Numerator, denominator and period for the 85% activity-coverage claim
Timed record of the 8-to-4-hour monthly task and the number of Sonar projects actually evaluated
Proof the fine-tuned model was deployed or served any run, plus an independent frozen holdout comparison against the base model
Any stakeholder or service-user outcome measure

reasons: N1 2: N01 shows 104.6% of the test volume target and a failed P90 check (four samples per transaction). That demonstrates detection, not requirements met. No passing acceptance or closure record exists.

N2 2: Deriving workloads from production traffic, AKS autoscaling and six profiles are described in a digest. One workload visual is transcribed. Transaction mix, environment comparability and the production baseline are unresolved.
N3 2: Three releases are reported without dates, acceptance records or an observation window. The 90% effort savings have no baseline. Dashboards are described, not evidenced as release inputs.
N4 2: Goals, resources and scope are clear and attributed. Every quantified achievement is narrative-reported (N03, N04), except the transcribed workload and alert values.

N5 3: Strongest criterion. The paper sets out the telemetry gap (57/64 missing, 11% available, correctly framed), the cache-reproduction method, data-rebuild handling and exit-state fixes as clear challenge-and-response pairs. No retest numbers exist, so it caps below 4.
editorial_fixes: Cache section: 'A production service experienced excessive cache growth following repeated requests to a public endpoint.' is unattributed. Replace with: 'The case narrative reports that a production service experienced excessive cache growth following repeated requests to a public endpoint (N02).'

Data-generator paragraph cites N04, but N04's locators and digest do not cover the generator, exit-state fixes or storage-key retrieval. Either add the correct source locator or remove the citation and attribute to 'the delivery narrative' with the source identified in the evidence index.
Telemetry paragraph: 'on runs that had previously appeared successful' is not in the N04 digest. Retain it only if the source paragraph supports it; otherwise delete the phrase.
Cross-paper: state in the AI-assisted engineering paragraph 'This entry claims no separate saving from that assistance.' This prevents a reader from assuming Copilot effort is counted in both papers.

Consider generalising 'identity migration' and 'identity performance suite' to 'a platform migration' and 'a service performance suite' if organiser confidentiality treats the service type as identifying.
missing_evidence: Timed before/after records for performance and infrastructure validation, including review and exception effort
Passing acceptance run, remediation retest and closure for the failed P90 transactions, with adequate sample sizes
Production baseline for the 125% label and the 50x capacity claim
Matched baseline and retest numbers for the cache case (growth or memory, response, errors, change identifier, acceptance)
Release dates, acceptance records and a defined post-release observation window for the three releases
Telemetry gate failure and recovery run records, and raw output for the 285 tooling tests
Redacted primary visuals suitable for upload, with identifiers removed

reasons: I1 2: Service-owned tagged scenarios feeding shared regression is a coherent ownership model. The paper itself concedes it applies an established mechanism, and no records show practice changed.

I2 2: The driver (central team cannot hold every service's domain knowledge) and the three-pipeline and template design are clear. The implementation is narrative-only; no code or pipeline history was inspected.

I3 1: No comparative contribution is offered, and no substantiated attempt to go beyond existing industry practice. The paper explicitly states that wider adoption and comparative impact are not established.
I4 1: Goals and resources are stated. There are no results: five teams is reported participation, no onboarding saving is claimed, and no coverage or maintenance benefit is measured.
I5 2: The maintenance obligation, triage routing and failure-artefact retention are well reasoned. No completed failure-to-owner-to-rerun example exists.
editorial_fixes: Fix an internal inconsistency. Section 4 says 'The source describes five service teams using the onboarding approach (S02).' S02 and Section 1 say five teams on the shared platform. Replace with: 'The source describes five service teams on the shared platform (S02).'

Section 2: 'The team responsible for a failure can inspect the evidence without relying on the individual machine used to start a test.' Present tense implies observed operation. Replace with: 'In this design, the team responsible for a failure can inspect the evidence without relying on the individual machine used to start a test.'
Section 1: 'The platform pipeline selects those scenarios from contributing repositories' should be prefixed 'As described in the source,' to stay consistent with the attribution used elsewhere.
Summary: 'a reusable ownership and execution method' becomes 'an ownership and execution method designed for reuse', since reuse beyond this platform is not shown.
Section 3 could strengthen I3 without new facts by contrasting the model explicitly with a centrally authored regression pack, as a stated design difference. It must not claim industry novelty.
missing_evidence: Repository and pipeline implementation records for the tag convention, three pipelines and template generator
Per-team contribution history and shared-regression run records demonstrating active adoption by the five teams
One complete contributed-scenario failure, owner assignment, correction and rerun
Like-for-like onboarding timing covering the same steps and validation effort
Measured regression benefit (duplicate maintenance avoided, coverage, defects caught) against prior practice
Any comparative or external evidence supporting I3; external adoption is not the only route, but some substantiated comparison is needed

council_recommendation: No new evidence was introduced in round three; the changes are wording only, and no evidence mark rises for prose. All three papers are now largely honest about scope. The residual errors listed above are attribution and consistency fixes that need no new facts. All three papers have reached an evidence plateau: 4/5 on every criterion is not defensible for any paper on the current pack, and further editing cannot close the gap. Can be packaged now: A01-A09 with their scope notes (A09 retained as adverse evidence), N01-N04 and S01-S02 as source digests with hashes. Hashes prove file identity, not the truth of claims. Cannot be packaged until acquired: primary ledgers, timed comparisons, run and acceptance records, retest numbers, contribution histories and quality comparisons. Cross-paper conflicts: (1) the AI-assisted dashboard and script work in the NFT paper may overlap the AI paper's account-wide Copilot savings; state that the NFT paper claims no separate saving. (2) The account AI savings, the NFT work and shared regression involve different populations, and a common nomination or project boundary is not established. Each entry should define its own project boundary. (3) The PerfOps vs Inteliperf boundary is now handled correctly. Third-party client identity must be supplied to organisers through the separate route; anonymity in the text is not an exemption. Recommendation: do not submit expecting 4/5 scores. Either acquire the primary records listed, or submit with the current honest framing and accept scores near 2/5.
